title: Geometric scalar extension of a split simply connected semisimple root datum
statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic zero [def-weil-field], with algebraic closure $F$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $k$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme]. Suppose $G$ is semisimple: over $F$ there is no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal subgroup, where solvable means that successive commutator subgroup schemes become trivial. Suppose $G$ is simply connected: every surjective homomorphism $G'\to G$ from a connected semisimple $k$-group with finite central kernel is an isomorphism; finite central means a finite-dimensional coordinate algebra and commutation after every scalar extension. Let $T\subseteq G$ be a split maximal torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], meaning a closed subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$, maximal among tori after extension to $F$. Here $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$. Put $X=\operatorname{Hom}_k(T,\mathbf G_m)$ and $Y=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\mathbf G_m,T)$ with pairing $\chi\circ\eta(t)=t^{\langle\chi,\eta\rangle}$. Write $\Phi\subset X$ for the nonzero adjoint $T$-weights on $\operatorname{Lie}(G)=T_eG$ and $\alpha^\vee\in Y$ for the coroots normalized by the opposite root subgroups. Fix a simple-root base $\Delta$, meaning a linearly independent set of roots such that every root has integer coordinates in it all of one sign, and let $\Phi^+$ be those with nonnegative coordinates.

Then $G_F=G\times_k F$ is smooth connected affine semisimple and simply connected over $F$, and $T_F$ is a split maximal torus. Extending characters and cocharacters gives bijections from $X,Y$ to the character and cocharacter lattices of $T_F$, preserving their integer pairing and identifying the roots, coroots and their reflections. The natural $T_F$-equivariant tangent isomorphism $F\otimes_k\operatorname{Lie}(G)\simeq\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)$ carries $F\otimes_k\operatorname{Lie}(G)_\alpha$ onto the corresponding root space. There exists a Borel subgroup $B\subseteq G_F$ containing $T_F$ whose positive roots are exactly the specified $\Phi^+$. Here Borel means maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup. If $U$ is its largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup (unipotent means unipotent matrices at geometric points in a faithful representation), then $B=U\rtimes T_F$ and $\operatorname{Lie}(U)=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)_\alpha$. The assertion includes rank zero.

source.place: 21.11--21.12, printed pp.428--430 (roots and normalized coroots); 21.29--21.35, printed pp.433--435 (chosen positive system and Borel); 23.56, 23.58--23.59, printed pp.501--502 (field-independent split root datum and simply connected weight lattice).

proof.text: Smoothness and affineness persist under $k\to F$ by [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](1),(2). Since the coordinate algebra is finitely generated, its scalar extension is generated by the same finite list, so $G_F$ is of finite type. The identity is a $k$-point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] gives connectedness after every field extension. The assumed absence of smooth connected solvable normal subgroups says precisely that $G_F$ is semisimple. By [lem-sfb-smooth-unipotent-solvable], a smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup $N$ of $G_F$ has a subnormal series $N=N_0\supseteq\cdots\supseteq N_s=1$ with commutative quotients; every commutator of $N_i$ maps to $1$ in $N_i/N_{i+1}$, so the commutator subgroup scheme of $N_i$ lies in $N_{i+1}$, and inductively the $i$-th commutator subgroup scheme of $N$ lies in $N_i$. Thus $N$ is solvable in the sense of the hypothesis, hence trivial, and $G_F$ is reductive. Applying [lem-sfb-geometric-neutral-reductivity-field-invariance] to $G$ shows that every geometric fibre over $k$ is reductive. The smooth affine criterion [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] supplies finite presentation. Thus $G/\operatorname{Spec}k$ satisfies the reductive-group hypotheses used below. Splitness of $T_F$ is obtained by base changing the given isomorphism with $\mathbf G_m^r$, and its maximality is part of the hypothesis on $T$.

source.place: Propositions 1.34, 19.13 and definitions in Chapter 19; geometric semisimplicity is the hypothesis. Affine smoothness: Stacks Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize; Tag 02H6, lemma-smooth-formally-smooth; base change: Tags 01SD and 01V7.

proof.text: Fix $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. By [lem-sfb-relative-split-torus-matrix-sheaf], characters are integer row vectors and cocharacters are integer column vectors, over both $k$ and $F$. Scalar extension leaves these vectors unchanged, so gives the required bijections on $X$ and $Y$. Composition is matrix multiplication; hence $\langle(a_i),(b_i)\rangle=\sum_i a_ib_i$ over both fields. This also proves that the pairing is perfect and identifies $Y$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z}(X,\mathbf Z)$. The calculation permits $r=0$.

source.place: Theorem 12.9(a), printed pp.233-234; monomial maps and their compositions.

proof.text: The tangent comparison of [lem-sfb-affine-group-lie-tangent-calculus] gives $F\otimes_k\mathfrak g\simeq\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)$. It respects conjugation: on dual-number points the comparison sends a tangent vector represented by $e+\epsilon v$ to the same point after scalar extension, and $t(e+\epsilon v)t^{-1}=e+\epsilon\operatorname{Ad}(t)v$ over every test algebra. Thus it is $T_F$-equivariant. Apply [lem-sfb-relative-torus-bundle-weights] to the adjoint coaction: its $m$-weight space is exactly $F\otimes_k\mathfrak g_m$. A nonzero finite-dimensional weight space stays nonzero, since a basis vector extends to a basis vector over $F$; the zero space stays zero. Consequently the bijection on characters identifies precisely the nonzero adjoint weights, namely the roots, and gives the asserted root-space isomorphisms.

source.place: 10.19-10.21, printed pp.192-193; Section 21(a), printed pp.424-425, adjoint weight decomposition.

proof.text: For applying [lem-sfb-arbitrary-base-root-lines-coroots] over $k$, the geometric maximal-torus condition holds over every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$. Indeed [lem-sfb-reductive-torus-self-centralizer] gives $C_G(T)=T$ as subgroup functors, and the same equality over $\Omega$ follows by evaluating it on $\Omega$-algebras. A torus containing $T_\Omega$ is commutative, so lies in this centralizer and equals $T_\Omega$. The root-lines lemma now gives one-dimensional geometric root spaces and identifies the normalized coroot for each root after arbitrary base change. A weight space over a field whose dimension becomes one over $F$ is already one-dimensional (extend a basis). Thus each $\alpha\in\Phi$ has rank-one weight module over $k$, and the lemma applies to $k\to F$. It identifies $\alpha^\vee_F$ with the coroot of $\alpha_F$ in the opposite-root normalization. Finally $s_\alpha(x)=x-\langle x,\alpha^\vee\rangle\alpha$ and $s_\alpha(y)=y-\langle\alpha,y\rangle\alpha^\vee$ commute with the lattice bijections by step 2, so the reflections are identified as well.

source.place: Theorem 21.11(e) and Corollary 21.12, printed pp.429-430; coroot uniqueness and normalization. The relative base-change result is the cited existing root-lines node.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-semisimple-weight-lattice-criterion] over $k$. The assumed central-isogeny definition of simple connectedness implies $X=P(\Phi)$. Steps 2-4 identify $X_F\otimes\mathbf Q$ with $X\otimes\mathbf Q$ and every integrality test $\langle v,\alpha^\vee\rangle\in\mathbf Z$ on these spaces. Hence they identify $P(\Phi_F)$ with $P(\Phi)$ and give $X_F=P(\Phi_F)$. Apply the reverse implication of the same criterion over $F$ (also of characteristic zero): every central isogeny to $G_F$ from a connected semisimple group is an isomorphism. This proves precisely the simply connected clause without assuming that such an isogeny descends to $k$.

source.place: Propositions 23.29 and 23.59, printed pp.493 and 502; field-independent diagrams in 23.56-23.58.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-semisimple-roots-span] for $G_F$, the roots span $V=X_F\otimes\mathbf Q$. The specified linearly independent $\Delta_F$ spans $V$, since every root has integral coordinates in it. Define the rational linear functional $f$ on this basis by $f(\delta)=1$ for each $\delta\in\Delta_F$. For any root, its coefficients all have one sign and are not all zero, so $f(\alpha)>0$ exactly when $\alpha\in\Phi_F^+$. Perfectness from step 2 identifies $f$ with an element of $Y_F\otimes\mathbf Q$. In an integer basis of $Y_F$, choose a positive common denominator $N$ of its finitely many coordinates. Then $\lambda=Nf\in Y_F$ is a cocharacter and $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle$ has precisely the required sign for every root. Thus $\lambda$ is regular. If the rank is zero, $V=0$, take $f=0$ and $\lambda=0$; all the conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Definition 21.26 and Propositions 21.29-21.31, pp.433-434; rational chamber contains an integral cocharacter. Explicit denominator argument written here.

proof.text: Set $B=P(\lambda)$ using [lem-sfb-regular-cocharacter-borel-description]. It is a Borel containing $T_F$, and its roots are exactly those with $\langle\alpha,\lambda\rangle>0$, hence exactly the specified $\Phi_F^+$. For this pair, [lem-sfb-reductive-borel-pair-structure] identifies the largest smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup $U=R_u(B)$ and gives $B=U\rtimes T_F$. By [lem-sfb-borel-root-product-coordinates], multiplication identifies the product of the positive root subgroups with $U$, equivariantly under $T_F$. These factors are the root subgroups $U_\alpha$ of [lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations], and that statement characterizes $U_\alpha$ as the subgroup normalized by $T_F$ whose tangent space is $\mathfrak g_\alpha$. Differentiating this finite product map at the identity sends $(v_\alpha)$ to $\sum v_\alpha$: on dual numbers multiplication of tangent points is addition. Since the map is an isomorphism, its tangent map is an isomorphism. Thus $\operatorname{Lie}(U)=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Phi_F^+}\mathfrak g_\alpha$ as the specified subspace of $\operatorname{Lie}(G_F)$. Empty roots give $P(0)=T_F=G_F$ and the empty-product result $U=1$, so this also proves the rank-zero case.

source.place: Proposition 21.29, Theorem 21.32, Definition 21.35, pp.433-435; Theorem 21.68(a),(b), printed p.445; Theorem 21.11(c), pp.429-430.

proof_origin.place: Chapters 12, 19, 21 and 23, especially 21.11-21.12, 21.29-21.35, 21.68(a),(b), 23.29 and 23.59. Explicit lattice transport and denominator calculation assemble the cited results.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q12-2c26be167 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 7 steps, the new node lem-sfb-split-semisimple-weight-lattice-criterion and the statement of every cited node. I checked the new node against Milne (2017): Def 18.5, Prop 19.15, Prop 23.29 (p.493), Thm 23.55/Cor 23.56 (p.501) and Prop 23.59 (p.502). Prop 23.59 holds over any field, so the new node, which only needs characteristic 0, is a faithful special case. I tested it on rank 0, SL2 (X=P) and PGL2 (X=Zα≠P, with SL2→PGL2 as the counterexample isogeny); both directions agree in each case. It duplicates no existing node: the nearby ones (simply-connected-character-lattice and others) work over an algebraically closed field, give one direction only, or are constructions. It is not a clause of the item, which never states X=P(Φ). Step 5 is not circular: over F it uses only the reverse direction, and the hypothesis that direction needs is proved first. Step 4's hypotheses (reductive over arbitrary base; maximal geometric tori through C_G(T)=T) are established in steps 1 and 4. Steps 2 and 3 cite exactly the base-change clauses they use. Step 6's integral regular cocharacter calculation is written out, and rank 0 is handled. I made two citation and gap repairs in the item file. (1) Step 7 cited reductive-rank-one-reflections for the tangent spaces of the root-subgroup factors U_α, but that node only gives some root subgroup with Lie algebra g_α (C4). I replaced it in the step and in proof_deps by lem-sfb-reductive-root-subgroup-parametrizations; that node is a stmt_dep of borel-root-product-coordinates and characterizes U_α by Lie(U_α)=g_α. (2) Step 1 now writes out how the subnormal-series solvability of smooth-unipotent-solvable gives the derived-series solvability in the hypothesis. The statement is unchanged. Batch-5 flags: all nine citations are reductive-group structure theory. Their closure reaches sec-trace-formula only through generic descent and lattice lemmas (fppf/fpqc, smooth fpqc descent, cover descent datum, f.g. torsion-free free, split lattice torus projection), none of which is part of the trace formula or Poincaré duality, so I accepted them.
